chunks: He said: Indeed, Allah, the Exalted, is not a wrongdoer to His servants, nor unaware of them, nor denying His favors, nor cutting off His mercy, nor breaking His promise, nor contrary to His word, nor unaware of them, nor unjust to them, nor denying His favors, nor cutting off His mercy, nor breaking His promise, nor contrary to His word.
ai.seo_question: What are the key attributes of Allah regarding justice and mercy towards His servants?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq uses this hadith to ground the doctrine of divine justice (*Adl*) within the broader framework of Allah’s attributes, linking His justice and knowledge to His covenantal faithfulness (*Wafa’*). This reinforces the Shia theological emphasis that God’s mercy and promises are not arbitrary but are intrinsically tied to His perfect wisdom and awareness of His servants. Such affirmations serve to strengthen the believer’s trust (*Tawakkul*) in divine retribution and reward.
